parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderService is an application service: it runs use cases and coordinates two aggregates. The core business rules are delegated to the domain: reserve, release, dispatch and toStockLevel in domain/product, and nextState, assertCancellable and isOrderStatus in domain/order. Persistence goes only through injected ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository), and the file contains no HTTP, framework or storage code. The all-or-nothing rollback is a transaction concern, which belongs in an application layer. Triggering dispatch when an order moves to shipped is cross-aggregate coordination, which is also application work. Some rules sit in placeOrder rather than the domain: the order must have at least one line, quantities must be positive integers, duplicate lines are merged, and the new order is built with status "placed". cancel also sets the status directly. This leans toward an anemic domain, but these are input checks and order setup, which an application layer can reasonably do. None of them is a responsibility of a different layer kind under the rubric.
